_comment: WORK slider -> project detail pages. project.html?p=<slug> reads this file and renders one entry. 'hero'/'media' items are {src, kind, caption} — kind is 'image' (default) or 'video'; missing/null src falls back to the halftone placeholder, same convention as the gallery. 'media' items may set 'full': true to span the full width instead of sitting in the 2-up grid. 'credits' is a flat label/value list. 'preview' is a plain src string for the homepage spotlight carousel only (grayscale, landscape-cropped) — the project page always uses 'hero' instead.

projects.title: Young Fashion Stars
projects.headline: Fashion school portraits shot from directly above, every model looking straight up into the light.
body: Mattoni's scholarship show for graduating designers needed portraits that could stand next to the runway work itself — so we shot each collection from a single fixed angle, straight down, the model looking back up into the lens. It flattens the runway pose into something closer to a mugshot, which felt right for clothes built to be examined rather than just worn.
One studio, one light, one wall — the same setup repeated for every designer in the lineup, so the only thing that changes frame to frame is the collection itself.

projects.title: Bolt Food
projects.headline: Portraits of the riders who actually deliver — shot on their own routes, not a studio.
body: The brief covered the whole fleet: the bag on a back, on a bike, on a scooter, crossing the same Prague streets the riders cross every shift. Nothing staged beyond asking each one to hold still for a second between drops.
Cast from real couriers rather than models, on location across the city rather than in front of a backdrop, so the campaign reads as a shift log rather than an ad.

projects.title: Mattoni
projects.headline: A day inside Mattoni's Malacky plant, following the people who bottle it rather than the water.
body: For a campaign built on the word "authentic," we spent the shoot on the production floor and in the break room rather than at a product table — pallets, forklifts, the same fluorescent-lit office where the interviews actually happened.

The crew stays visible in half the frames on purpose: a boom mic, a reflector, someone checking a monitor. The point was never to hide that it's a shoot, only to make sure what's in front of the camera is real.

projects.title: Foodora
projects.headline: A rooftop commercial shoot that ended with a gold egg by the pool.
body: Half the day was riders and bikes against Prague's business district; the other half turned into whatever the art department could build on a hotel terrace, reflectors bouncing straight sun into every corner. Fisheye throughout, because the crew ended up in as many frames as the talent.
Loosest brief of the year: bring the bike, bring the bag, see where the day goes. It went to a golden egg.
